## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: multi-container pod design, InitContainers, PVCs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, TLS sidecars, probes, PDBs, and network policies, plus load validation and rollback strategies.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer for tooling setup
- PVC mounting and data direction between /data/events and /data/enriched
- ConfigMap/Secret for runtime config and credentials
- TLS sidecar for certificate rotation
- Readiness and Liveness probes
- PodDisruptionBudget
- NetworkPolicy for scoped egress
- Load testing and rollback workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator-config
data:
  batchSize: "100"
  enrichmentEndpoint: "http://enrich-controller.analytics.svc.cluster.local:8080/enrich"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  apiToken: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-aggregator
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-aggregator
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: init-tools
          image: alpine:3.17
          command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl jq; sleep 0"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: myrepo/config-aggregator:latest
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: config-aggregator-config
            - secretRef:
                name: config-aggregator-creds
          volumeMounts:
            - name: events
              mountPath: /data/events
            - name: enriched
              mountPath: /data/enriched
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 9000
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: 9000
            initialDelaySeconds: 20
            periodSeconds: 10
      volumes:
        - name: events
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: config-aggregator-events-pvc
        - name: enriched
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: config-aggregator-enriched-pvc
```

- How would you adapt this for namespace isolation across multiple environments?
- What scaling considerations arise with batchSize tuning and backpressure?
- How would you observe and debug under intermittent enrichment endpoint failures?

## Code Example

```yaml
# 1) RBAC: roles for VolumeSnapshots
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: volumesnapshots-access
  namespace: backups
rules:
- apiGroups: ["snapshot.storage.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["volumesnapshots", "volumesnapshots/status"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "delete", "update"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: volumesnapshots-access-binding
  namespace: backups
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: backups-sa
  namespace: backups
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: volumesnapshots-access
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
# 2) CronJob to create VolumeSnapshot
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: backups-snapshot-cron
  namespace: backups
spec:
  schedule: "0 */6 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: backups-sa
          containers:
          - name: snapshotter
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh","-c","kubectl apply -f - << 'YAML'\napiVersion: snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1\nkind: VolumeSnapshot\nmetadata:\n  name: data-pvc-snap-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)\nspec:\n  volumeSnapshotClassName: csi-snap-class\n  source:\n    persistentVolumeClaimName: data-pvc\nYAML"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
---
# 3) Job to restore from a snapshot
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: data-pvc-restore
  namespace: backups
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 3600
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: restore
        image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","kubectl delete pvc data-pvc-restore-<ts> 2>/dev/null || true; kubectl apply -f - << 'YAML2'\napiVersion: v1\nkind: PersistentVolumeClaim\nmetadata:\n  name: data-pvc-restore-<ts>\nspec:\n  dataSource:\n    kind: VolumeSnapshot\n    apiGroup: snapshot.storage.k8s.io\n    name: data-pvc-snap-<ts>\n  accessModes: [\"ReadWriteOnce\"]\n  resources:\n    requests:\n      storage: 1Gi\nYAML2"]
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose Kubernetes primitives for practical automation: CronJobs, Jobs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and PVCs, plus robust scheduling and rollback.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and jobTemplate usage
- ConfigMap and Secret as environment sources
- PVC mounting in Jobs for persistent backups
- Concurrency policy and job history controls
- Rollback and validation workflows

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-backup
  namespace: dataops
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 7
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 7200
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: postgres-backup
            image: postgres:15
            env:
            - name: BACKUP_DIR
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: backup-config
                  key: BACKUP_DIR
            - name: DB_HOST
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: backup-config
                  key: DB_HOST
            - name: DB_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-credentials
                  key: DB_USER
            - name: DB_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-credentials
                  key: DB_PASSWORD
            command:
            - /bin/bash
            - -c
            - |
              DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d)
              BACKUP_FILE="/backups/${DB_NAME}-${DATE}.sql"
              pg_dump -h $DB_HOST -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME > $BACKUP_FILE
            volumeMounts:
            - name: backup-storage
              mountPath: /backups
          volumes:
          - name: backup-storage
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: backup-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Validation Plan
1. Check CronJob creation: `kubectl get cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
2. Verify schedule: `kubectl describe cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
3. Test manual job: `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/db-backup test-backup -n dataops`
4. Monitor job completion: `kubectl get jobs -n dataops -w`
5. Validate backup files: `kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -n dataops -- ls -la /backups`

## Rollback Plan
1. Delete CronJob: `kubectl delete cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
2. Clean up test jobs: `kubectl delete jobs -l job-name=db-backup -n dataops`
3. Remove backup files if needed: Access PVC and delete specific backup files
4. Recreate with corrected manifest if issues persist

## Why This Is Asked

- Shared volumes and proper MountPaths
- Sidecar pattern for log shipping

- Rollback strategy and safe deploys

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal patch sketch
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: processor
  namespace: payments
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: fix-permissions
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/logs"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /mnt/logs
      containers:
      - name: processor
        image: your-registry/processor:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: in-data
          mountPath: /data/input
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log/processor
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "256Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /readyz
            port: 8080
      - name: log-shipper
        image: busybox:stable
        command: ["sh", "-c", "tail -F /var/log/processor/app.log | nc log-collector 10514"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log/processor
        - name: ship
          mountPath: /var/log/ship
      volumes:
      - name: in-data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: processor-input-pvc
      - name: logs
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: ship
```

## Why This Is Asked
Auditors assess knowledge of Kubernetes pod security hardening and defense-in-depth strategies.

## Key Concepts
- Pod securityContext vs container securityContext
- runAsNonRoot enforcement and UID requirements
- readOnlyRootFilesystem and volume mount implications
- Capability dropping and privilege escalation controls
- Seccomp profiles via annotations and runtime defaults
- Rolling update safety and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```yaml
# Security hardening patch for collector Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: collector
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod: runtime/default
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 1000
        fsGroup: 2000
      containers:
      - name: collector
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - ALL
          volumeMounts:
          - name: input
            mountPath: /data/input
          - name: output
            mountPath: /data/output
        # Preserve existing probes and resources
        # livenessProbe, readinessProbe, resources remain unchanged
```

## Validation & Rollback
**Validation:**
- `kubectl get pods -n apps -l app=collector -o yaml | grep securityContext`
- `kubectl auth can-i create pods --as=system:serviceaccount:apps:collector`
- Test pod startup and volume access
- Verify non-root execution: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- id`

**Rollback:**
- `kubectl rollout undo deployment/collector -n apps`
- Monitor rollout status: `kubectl rollout status deployment/collector -n apps`
- Document security context changes in version control

```yaml
  name: python-api

spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: python-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: python-api
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-deps
        image: python:3.11-alpine

        volumeMounts:
        - name: app-code
          mountPath: /app
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: python:3.11-alpine
        command: ['python', '/app/main.py']
        env:

        - name: API_USERNAME
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: api-credentials
              key: username
        - name: API_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: api-credentials
              key: password
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health

          periodSeconds: 20
        volumeMounts:
        - name: app-code
```

- **Namespace Isolation**: Per-namespace design improves security boundaries but requires duplicate configuration management

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical security hardening and disruption management capabilities for CKAD-level Kubernetes deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Container SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem for container isolation
- PodSecurityContext: fsGroup for proper file permissions on PVC-mounted volumes
- Kernel capabilities: drop ALL to minimize attack surface
- PodDisruptionBudget: maintain minimum healthy pods during maintenance
- Rollout and rollback procedures for safe deployments

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
  labels:
    app: api-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api-gateway
    spec:
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1001
      containers:
      - name: api-gateway
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - "ALL"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /srv
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/app
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: api-gateway-pvc
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: api-gateway-config
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api-gateway-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-gateway
```

## Verification & Rollback
```bash
# Verify under load
kubectl exec deployment/api-gateway -- curl http://localhost:8080/health
kubectl top pods -l app=api-gateway
kubectl get pods -l app=api-gateway --watch

# Rollback if needed
kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway
kubectl rollout status deployment/api-gateway
```
